description: WEEKLY WINDOW + AGE GATE INTERACTION. `schedule` is Monday-only, and Renovate can only create, rebase, or merge a branch while it is inside that window — an out-of-schedule run is a no-op (verified 2026-08-12: caltex-landing's 12:52 UTC run logged `Repository finished / result: done` with zero branch activity). Pair that with a top-level `minimumReleaseAge` and an automerge-eligible group can miss its own window: the PR opens Monday carrying a pending `renovate/stability-days` status because the release is younger than the gate at creation time, the status clears on Tuesday, and by then Renovate will not touch the branch again until the following Monday. Observed on reddoor-maintenance#509, which stayed green, CLEAN and unmerged across four Renovate runs including two manual dispatches.

`prCreation: not-pending` with `internalChecksFilter: strict` is Renovate's documented answer: pending releases are filtered out of the candidate set, and the PR is only opened once nothing about it is pending, so every PR Renovate opens can merge inside the same window that opened it. A release landing too close to the window waits for the next Monday instead of opening a PR that cannot merge — the same end-to-end latency as before, without a confusing PR sitting open and unmergeable in between. `internalChecksFilter` is already Renovate's default and is pinned only so this fleet-wide contract does not depend on an unstated upstream default.

CORRECTION (2026-09-21): #28 TOOK TWO OF THE THREE OPTIONS RENOVATE'S DOCS PRESCRIBE, AND THE MISSING ONE STOPPED EVERY ROUTINE PR IN THE FLEET FOR 40 DAYS. The paragraph above calls `prCreation: not-pending` with `internalChecksFilter: strict` 'Renovate's documented answer'. The documented answer has a third part, printed as a warning under `minimumReleaseAge`: 'If your CI runs only on pull_request events (so Renovate branches have no checks), also set internalChecksAsSuccess=true so the release-age check can turn the branch green - otherwise PR creation may be deferred indefinitely.' That is this fleet exactly. CI runs on `pull_request` only, so a Renovate branch carries one status, Renovate's own `renovate/stability-days`, and zero check runs; Renovate does not count its own statuses toward the branch status unless `internalChecksAsSuccess` is true, so the branch read as pending on every run and no PR was created. Measured 2026-09-20: the last `renovate/all-minor-patch` PR anywhere in the fleet was created 2026-08-10 and the last one merged 2026-08-12, the day #28 landed; the fleet-security sweep printed `RENOVATE_OUTCOME drought=20 delivering=1`; sites sat on `@reddoorla/maintenance` 0.81 to 0.95 against 0.98 published. What hid it: lock-file-maintenance PRs kept appearing (gallerysonder#88, created 2026-08-31), because that update type is exempt from `minimumReleaseAge`, carries no stability status, and so falls through to the 25-hour `prNotPendingHours` timeout, which the grouped branch, rebased every Monday inside an 18-hour window, never reaches. Proven on one repo before it shipped here, both arms inside the same Monday window (2026-09-21 UTC). PASS arm, reddoor-starter with the option set in its own renovate.json (reddoor-starter#154, merged 02:23Z): its first run afterwards rebased every branch onto the moved main and opened nothing, which is Renovate's ordinary early return on any run that pushes a commit while `prCreation` is not `immediate`, so PR creation is only ever attempted on a run that pushes nothing; its second run, 02:28Z, pushed nothing and opened reddoor-starter#155 (`renovate/all-minor-patch`), #156 and #157, the first routine Renovate PRs anywhere in the fleet since 2026-08-10. Control, espada on the unchanged preset: its 01:57Z scheduled run rebased `renovate/all-minor-patch` at 01:58Z and opened no PR, and a second run at 02:28Z, from a branch state identical to the starter's (tip on current main, `renovate/stability-days: success`, zero check runs, dashboard 'Pending Status Checks'), pushed nothing and again opened nothing. `validate.yml` now refuses `prCreation: not-pending` without `internalChecksAsSuccess: true`. Note that invariant (1) below was written the same day as #28, and #28 broke it anyway: the option that left the PR pending at creation time was `prCreation` itself. EXPECT A WAVE: the first in-window run after this lands opens roughly six weeks of held PRs in every repo (one grouped minor/patch PR plus each pending major), throttled by `prHourlyLimit`. Groups containing a never-automerge package wait for a human, as designed.

THE SAFETY PROPERTY MOVED, AND THIS IS NOW INVARIANT (3) (2026-09-21). `internalChecksAsSuccess: true` also feeds the branch status Renovate uses for AUTOMERGE. Read from Renovate's source: PR creation under `not-pending` only happens on a run that pushed nothing (the two exceptions, artifact errors and a requested rebase, cannot be followed by a same-run merge), and on exactly those runs the branch worker goes straight on to `checkAutoMerge`; with this option true the platform layer no longer demotes an all-`renovate/` success set to pending, and with zero check runs registered it returns green. So for an automerge-eligible group Renovate ATTEMPTS THE MERGE IN THE SAME RUN THAT OPENS THE PR, before CI has started. Before 2026-08-12 a branch could never be green without real check runs, so Renovate itself waited for CI; now it does not, and what holds the merge back is GitHub refusing it because a required status check has not passed. Renovate then merges on a later run once CI is green: the same outcome as before, for a different reason. THEREFORE: every repo that extends this preset MUST have a required status check on every branch Renovate merges into, with no bypass actor for the reddoor-renovate App. Swept 2026-09-21: true of all 27 repos on their default branch (`ci / ci` on 25, `build`, `validate`; `bypass_actors` empty on all), and false of exactly one Renovate base branch, reddoor-website's `staging`, which the last packageRule covers. A repo bootstrapped without the ruleset, a bypass actor added, or a required check renamed so the rule no longer matches, would let an un-built dependency bump land unattended; the nightly protection audit is the instrument that has to catch that (reddoor-maintenance#892). Lock-file maintenance is NOT exposed UNDER THIS PRESET: with `minimumReleaseAge: null` and no merge confidence configured it carries no `renovate/` status, so its branch stays pending until real checks report. That is a property of this file, not of Renovate: enabling merge confidence adds a `renovate/merge-confidence` status that the same filter treats identically, and would expose it. The option that would restore the old property outright, rather than document its loss, is to run CI on `push` to `renovate/**` so Renovate branches carry real check runs.

LOCK-FILE MAINTENANCE OPENS ITS PR IMMEDIATELY (2026-10-19, reddoor-maintenance P1-52). The 2026-09-21 fix above reached every update type but this one. On 2026-10-19 all 15 maintained repos carried a `renovate/lock-file-maintenance` branch and none had an open lock-file PR; the newest merged one was medical-solutions-of-texas#65 (2026-09-15), and 29-navy and vida-legacy-foundation had never had one. A lock-file branch carries no status and no check run (fleet CI runs on `pull_request` only, and `minimumReleaseAge: null` gives it no `renovate/stability-days`), so its combined status is `pending` with no contexts and Renovate's GitHub platform returns yellow for it whatever `internalChecksAsSuccess` says. Under `prCreation: not-pending` two paths in Renovate 44.151.2 then refuse the PR. (1) A run that pushes a commit to a branch with no PR returns before PR creation whenever `prCreation` is not `immediate` (`Branch status pending, current sha`). (2) A run that pushes nothing reaches `ensurePr`, which skips a yellow branch younger than `prNotPendingHours` (25). The weekly refresh nearly always changes the lockfile, so the first Monday run rebuilds the branch (path 1) and every later in-window run finds it under 18 hours old (path 2); it is 25 hours old only outside the window, where Renovate creates no PR at all. Measured: erp-industrial's branch was rebuilt 2026-10-12 03:25Z and again 2026-10-19 02:30Z, and Renovate's own dry run with debug logging, on the unchanged preset inside the window, logged `Branch is 10 hours old - skipping PR creation as prNotPendingHours is set to 25` for it (erp-industrial#72, `control` arm). With `lockFileMaintenance.prCreation: immediate` added and nothing else changed, the same run logged `DRY-RUN: Would create PR: chore(deps): lock file maintenance`, and the two arms' full lists of actions differed by that one line (`immediate` arm). The option is set inside `lockFileMaintenance` only, so no other update type changes. It does not loosen the merge: the PR still merges only through Renovate's automerge check on a later run, which needs a green branch status, and with zero check runs and zero statuses that status stays yellow until CI reports; the required status check on the base branch (invariant 3) still holds it. `validate.yml` now refuses `prCreation: not-pending` without this.

GROUPED PRs OPEN IMMEDIATELY, AND THE HELD PACKAGES GROUP ALONE (2026-10-21). The two packageRules dated 2026-10-21 carry the why and the proof. EXPECT A WAVE: the first in-window run after this lands opens about four weeks of held grouped PRs at once, two per repo (`all-minor-patch`, automerge-eligible, and `held-minor-patch`, waiting for a human), throttled by `prHourlyLimit` (Renovate's default, 2 per hour), and out-of-schedule runs create no PR for a branch without one, so a repo's pending majors and lock-file maintenance can wait for the next Monday's run. Grouped PRs that used to wait for a human because they held `@reddoorla/maintenance` now merge unattended once CI is green, so invariant (3), a required status check on every base branch Renovate merges into, now carries about 20 more merges a week.

MAJORS OPEN ON THE RUN THAT PUSHES THEM, AND LOCK-FILE MAINTENANCE TAKES THE FIRST HOURLY PR SLOT (2026-10-24, reddoor-maintenance#1688). The two packageRules dated 2026-10-24 carry the why and the proof. Digests are deliberately NOT made immediate: a digest has no release timestamp, so under `minimumReleaseAge` (`timestamp-required`) its `renovate/stability-days` stays pending forever and `prCreation: not-pending` never creates its branch at all (`Skipping branch creation due to internal status checks not met`); made immediate, it opens behind that status and, because Renovate sorts digest ahead of patch and minor, takes an hourly PR slot ahead of both grouped PRs (reddoor-starter#208, `slots-test`: lock-file maintenance, then the digest, then neither grouped PR got a branch). So on this preset a digest update is never branched outside a security update, as it has been since `minimumReleaseAge` was set (read from Renovate's source, measured on reddoor-starter); turning digests on is a separate decision (reddoor-workspace decision 2026-10-24-1436). What `prHourlyLimit` (Renovate's default, 2) still means: in a week when both grouped branches refill, the Monday run opens lock-file maintenance and one grouped PR, and the other grouped PR and any new majors wait. The hourly count resets every clock hour (`getPrHourlyCount` counts PRs created since the hour began), so a second in-window run in a later hour would open them the same day. But the fleet's automatic runs are the 00:00Z and 12:00Z crons, and GitHub starts the 12:00Z one between 17:51Z and 21:12Z, almost always after `before 6pm on monday` closes (the 2026-10-21 minor/patch rule's measurement). So in practice they usually wait for the next Monday with a free slot, unless someone dispatches the workflow inside the window.

SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-08-12, same day as #28). #28's original text claimed the 2026-08-10 batch had frozen this way — '18 non-major PRs across the fleet sat CI-green, CLEAN and unmerged'. That was wrong, and the error is worth keeping visible because it is easy to repeat. 16 of those 17 site PRs were never automerge-eligible at all: `group:allNonMajor` had grouped `@reddoorla/maintenance` into each one, and the never-auto-merge packageRule below therefore applied to the whole grouped branch. They were correctly awaiting a human and a green Netlify deploy preview, exactly as designed. Only reddoor-maintenance#509 — the one group with no held package in it — was actually subject to the window/age interaction described above. The real blast radius is 'automerge-eligible groups', which on most weeks is a small number, not the fleet.

TWO INVARIANTS, both learned the hard way. (1) Any future option that can leave a PR pending at creation time must be checked against the Monday-only window before it ships: a gate that clears one day after the window closes is a gate that never opens. (2) Before calling a batch of open PRs 'stuck', check whether a packageRule is deliberately holding them. Under `group:allNonMajor` a single held package — `@reddoorla/maintenance` is in nearly every site's group — makes the entire grouped branch non-automergeable. A PR that is green, CLEAN and unmerged is far more often a rule working than a rule broken.

packageRules.description: Routine updates still merge unattended, but RENOVATE performs the merge from inside its own run — `platformAutomerge` is deliberately false. GitHub's platform auto-merge is a per-PR flag any write-access account can arm, and the PR then merges itself later with nobody watching; these rules have no authority over it. On 2026-07-26 a bulk `gh pr merge --auto` sweep armed it across 8 repos and two actions/checkout MAJORS merged with zero reviews the next morning (reddoor-starter#77, reddoor-website#111) once Renovate's rebase cleared their conflicts. Routing merges through Renovate makes these packageRules the actual decision-maker. Renovate can only merge while running, so the repo cron IS the merge cadence (twice daily).

Exempt lockfile maintenance from the top-level 1-day minimumReleaseAge. The gate (added in .github#26) emitted a pending renovate/stability-days status on every lock-file-maintenance PR, freezing all 11 of the 2026-08-10 Monday batch open and blocking the automerge that transitive-vuln cleanup rides on. CORRECTION (2026-08-12): the original version of this note justified the exemption by claiming fleet CI's pnpm supply-chain policy already rejects lockfile entries younger than 24h at install time. That is false — every fleet repo sets `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in pnpm-workspace.yaml (10/10 sampled, including reddoor-starter, which every site clones), so there is no pnpm-layer age gate backing this up. Do not cite one. The exemption stands on its own merits instead: lock-file maintenance re-resolves the ranges the manifest already permits rather than widening any range or adding a dependency, and it is the mechanism transitive-vulnerability cleanup rides on, so gating a whole-tree refresh on the freshest single transitive release trades real security latency for no meaningful supply-chain protection. `minimumReleaseAge: null` resets the option for this update type only (schema type is string|null, default null); normal version-bump PRs keep the 1-day wait, and security PRs were never gated (vulnerabilityAlerts defaults include minimumReleaseAge: null).

Never auto-merge packages that reshape the dependency graph (and thus pnpm hoisting). An @reddoorla/maintenance minor bump silently broke Netlify builds via an undeclared transitive sharp (fleet sharp fixes, 2026-06): GitHub Actions built green while Netlify failed. Require a human + a green Netlify deploy preview before these merge.

GROUPED MINOR/PATCH PRs OPEN ON THE RUN THAT PUSHES THEM (2026-10-21, reddoor-workspace decision 2026-10-21-2218, first written 2026-09-29 for reddoor-maintenance#898 and never applied). `group:allNonMajor` puts every minor and patch update into one `renovate/all-minor-patch` branch, so this rule reaches that branch and the held group below. Security branches already open immediately (Renovate's `vulnerabilityAlerts` defaults). Under the top-level `prCreation: not-pending`, a run that pushes a commit to a branch with no PR returns before PR creation (`!branchPr && commitSha && config.prCreation !== 'immediate'` in lib/workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts, Renovate 44.176.1), and the first Monday run nearly always pushes, because a week of releases has arrived. The PR could then open only on a second in-window run that pushed nothing, and the fleet gets one: the 00:00Z cron runs inside the window, and GitHub starts the 12:00Z one between 17:51Z and 21:12Z, so it almost always starts after `before 6pm on monday` closes at 18:00Z (alamo-anatomy's 17:51Z start on 10-19 was the one in-window exception, and it opened its PR). Measured 2026-10-21: 19 of 25 repos had no grouped PR opened since 09-22; hedloc's 10-19 run logged `Branch updated all-minor-patch` at 02:28Z and its next run started at 18:03Z. Proven on two repos, two arms each, real runs (reddoor-starter#197, canvas-starter#36): with this rule, `Branch created` and `PR created` for the grouped branch in the same run; without it, `Branch created` and then `Branch status pending, current sha`, and no PR. It does NOT make that run merge the PR: the same file skips automerge on any run that pushed (`config.ignoreTests === true || !commitSha`), so the merge happens on a later run, once CI has registered, and invariant (3) holds as before. Once the PR exists, out-of-schedule runs process it (`Branch + PR exists but is not scheduled -- will update if necessary`), so that merge need not wait a week. `internalChecksFilter: strict` still keeps releases younger than `minimumReleaseAge` out of the branch. This rule does not touch majors, lock-file maintenance or `prHourlyLimit`.

THE NEVER-AUTOMERGE PACKAGES GROUP ON THEIR OWN (2026-10-21, same decision). Under `group:allNonMajor` one held package made the whole grouped branch non-automergeable (invariant 2), and `@reddoorla/maintenance` is in the grouped list of 21 of 25 repos, so a grouped PR almost never automerged: medical-solutions-of-texas#68 and revogen#82 sat green and clean from 09-21. This rule moves the packages of the never-automerge rule above into a group of their own, `renovate/held-minor-patch` (base-prefixed on the staging flow), so the rest of `all-minor-patch` automerges through the rules above and only this small PR waits for a human and a green Netlify deploy preview. It keeps the reason for the hold and scopes it to the packages that need it. It matches minor and patch only, so their majors stay single PRs under the majors rule. Proven in a dry run on the same two repos: with it, `renovate/held-minor-patch` holds `@reddoorla/maintenance` (in the real run, with vulnerability alerts off, also `sharp` 0.35.4 to 0.35.5; in production `sharp` currently rides its security branch), and `renovate/all-minor-patch` logs `PR is configured for automerge`; without it the held packages stay in `all-minor-patch`, which logs `PR is not configured for automerge`. One cost, accepted: `@sveltejs/enhanced-img` now moves apart from the Vite and SvelteKit minors in `all-minor-patch`, so a version skew between them is possible for a week; CI catches a hard break, a Netlify-only break would show on the held PR's preview. validate.yml keeps this list equal to the never-automerge rule's: a package held there but missing here would hold the whole group again.

Majors need a human. This rule has been correct since the preset's first commit and was never the failure: Renovate has never armed auto-merge on a major. The 2026-07-26 incident (two actions/checkout majors merged with zero reviews — reddoor-starter#77, reddoor-website#111) came from a bulk `gh pr merge --auto` sweep by an operator/agent, which no Renovate config can block because platform auto-merge is a per-PR flag set outside Renovate. The real guard is that the fleet now disables platform auto-merge at the repository level (see the reddoor-maintenance `self-updating` recipe, which enforces allow_auto_merge=false and reports drift), so every merge goes through Renovate and lands on these rules. `platformAutomerge: false` here is belt-and-braces, not the mechanism.

MAJORS OPEN ON THE RUN THAT PUSHES THEM (2026-10-24, reddoor-maintenance#1688, reddoor-workspace decisions 2026-10-24-1413 and 2026-10-24-1436). The 2026-10-21 minor/patch rule above removed the drought's early return for grouped branches only: a run that pushes a commit to a branch with no PR returns before PR creation unless `prCreation` is `immediate` (`!branchPr && commitSha && config.prCreation !== 'immediate'`, lib/workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts), and the first in-window Monday run nearly always pushes, so a new major opened only in a week when a second in-window run pushed nothing (the full condition also lets a PR through on artifact errors or a requested rebase). Proven on reddoor-starter#208, real runs on Renovate 44.181.3, two arms with only majors and digests enabled and no hourly limit: without this rule, `Branch created` then `Branch status pending, current sha: 1e8c08b…` for `major-vitest-monorepo` and the same for `prismicio-svelte-3.x`, and no PR; with it, `Branch created` then `PR created` for both in the same run (reddoor-starter#217, #218). It does not loosen anything unattended: the majors rule above still sets `automerge: false`, so every major waits for a human as before; it only stops majors arriving weeks late. One edge it shares with digests: `immediate` also bypasses Renovate's skip for a branch it knows will stay pending, so a major whose datasource gives no release timestamp now opens behind a `renovate/stability-days` that never clears, where before it got no branch. The same bypass opens a major younger than `minimumReleaseAge` (1 day) at once, behind a pending `renovate/stability-days`; that status is not a required check, so the day's wait now holds only Renovate, not a human merging by hand. It still waits for a human, so the change is that it is visible sooner. It matches `major` only. Digests stay out, for the reason in the 2026-10-24 note at the top of this file, and validate.yml refuses `prCreation: immediate` on `digest`. It still competes for `prHourlyLimit`: majors sort after minor and patch, so in a week when both groups refill a new major usually waits for the next Monday with a free slot (the top note says why usually).

LOCK-FILE MAINTENANCE TAKES THE FIRST HOURLY PR SLOT (2026-10-24, reddoor-maintenance#1688, same decisions). Renovate creates at most `prHourlyLimit` PRs an hour (Renovate's default, 2; this preset does not set it), and for a branch without a PR, creation happens only in an in-window run, of which the fleet usually gets one a week (the top note), so every repo's two grouped PRs (`all-minor-patch`, `held-minor-patch`) compete with lock-file maintenance for two slots. Renovate processes branches in a fixed order: vulnerability alerts first, then by `prPriority` (higher first), then by update type in the order pin, digest, patch, minor, major, lockFileMaintenance (lib/workers/repository/process/sort.ts); once the hour's count is reached, every later branch logs `Hourly PRs limit reached`: one that does not exist yet is not created, and one that does is rebased but gets no PR (`Skipping PR - limit reached`). So lock-file maintenance, which went 30+ days without a PR until P1-52 (2026-10-19), lost to the groups in any week when both refilled and no second in-window run came. Proven on reddoor-starter#208, real runs on Renovate 44.181.3 with `prHourlyLimit: 2`: without this rule, `all-minor-patch` (#219) and `held-minor-patch` (#220) took both slots and `lock-file-maintenance` logged `Hourly PRs limit reached`; with it, `lock-file-maintenance` opened first (#216), `all-minor-patch` took the second slot (#221), and `held-minor-patch` waited. No more PRs per hour: it only reorders. `prPriority` is accepted only inside packageRules (Renovate's option schema, `parents: ['packageRules']`), not inside `lockFileMaintenance`. This rule must match `lockFileMaintenance` alone: one that also matched minor or patch would tie the grouped branches with it, and the update-type order would put them first again. validate.yml keeps it the highest `prPriority` in this file, on a rule of its own.

Hold pnpm at 11.8.x on EVERY surface it appears: pnpm/action-setup's self-installer crashes bootstrapping any pnpm >=11.9 target ('self-installer exits with code 1' / 'Cannot use in operator to search for integrity in undefined'), breaking CI fleet-wide (2026-07). Deliberately NOT scoped to matchDepTypes packageManager — the same dep also surfaces through the github-actions manager as pnpm/action-setup's `version:` input, and holding only one side ships a guaranteed failure: on 2026-08-03 reddoor-maintenance#492 bumped the workflow inputs to 11.18.0 against the held packageManager 11.8.0 and action-setup hard-errors on any version mismatch. (Workflows should not pass `version:` at all — packageManager is the single source of truth — but the hold must not depend on that discipline.) Only non-major pnpm bumps are held; MAJOR pnpm updates and vulnerabilityAlerts still open PRs so the operator is notified for a manual fleetwide bump. Remove when action-setup/corepack reliably installs pnpm >=11.9.

TypeScript 7 (the Go-based tsgo compiler) is rejected by typescript-eslint — every fleet CI hard-errors with 'typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.' (seen on the 2026-08-03 weekly batch: hedloc#27, caltex-landing#45). Keep TS on 6.x until typescript-eslint ships TS7 support, then delete this rule.

@libsql/kysely-libsql (the Kysely dialect reddoor-maintenance's hybrid DB runs on) hard-depends on @libsql/client ^0.8.0 and has no release supporting anything newer, so bumping the direct @libsql/client dep forks the tree into two incompatible Client types (typecheck: 'Promise<Replicated> is not assignable to Promise<void>', reddoor-maintenance#492 on the 2026-08-03 batch). Hold the client at 0.8.x until a kysely-libsql release widens its client range — Renovate will propose that release when it exists, and that PR is the cue to delete this rule and take both bumps together.

cookie v2 removed the parse/serialize named exports that every current @sveltejs/kit (<=2.70.2, cookie dep ^0.6.0) imports — forcing it via the vuln-wave overrides breaks the server build (rollup: 'parse is not exported by cookie@2.0.1', seen fleet-wide 2026-08-03). Worse, the range-WIDENING variant of the bump ('>=0.7.0 <3') is a delayed bomb: it stays on 0.7.x until the next lockfile-maintenance regen, then silently resolves to 2.x. Hold cookie below 2 until kit itself supports it, then delete this rule.

pnpm overrides are hand-managed security pins, never Renovate's to bump. Renovate misreads override KEYS as dependencies and proposes rewriting the pinned range itself: the 2026-08-03 'brace-expansion@<X to v5' wave (widening the override to <6 breaks minimatch@3/9 at runtime) and the 2026-08-10 'cookie@<0.7.0 to v1' wave (17 PRs fleet-wide; cookie 0.7.2 is already fully patched for GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x, so the rewrite adds zero security value and either flips @sveltejs/kit onto untested cookie 1.x or defers that jump to the next lockfile refresh). All three depTypes are listed because the npm manager assigns 'pnpm-workspace.overrides' to pnpm-workspace.yaml override entries (including flat 'parent>child' selector keys like '@sveltejs/kit>cookie'), 'pnpm.overrides' to package.json pnpm.overrides, and 'overrides' to package.json overrides; matching only 'overrides' would miss the workspace-YAML pins the fleet actually uses (pnpm 11 reads overrides from pnpm-workspace.yaml).

UNPROTECTED RENOVATE BASE BRANCH (2026-09-21). `internalChecksAsSuccess` also feeds the branch status Renovate uses for AUTOMERGE, and Renovate's docs say its default of false exists 'primarily to prevent automerge when the only check is a passing Renovate check'. Seconds after Renovate opens a PR, no CI check run is registered yet, so the only status is `renovate/stability-days: success` and the branch reads green. On a base branch with a REQUIRED status check GitHub refuses that merge and Renovate merges on a later run once CI is green, which is the designed path; swept 2026-09-21, all 27 repos extending this preset have a required check on their default branch (`ci / ci` on 25, `build`, `validate`). reddoor-website is the one exception: its renovate.json sets `baseBranchPatterns: ["staging"]`, and `staging` carries only a no-deletion ruleset, so an automerge-eligible minor/patch group (any week with no never-automerge package in it) could be merged into staging by Renovate before CI reported. This rule makes Renovate open those PRs and leave the merge to a human or an agent who has seen CI green. It is deliberately narrow: minor and patch are the only update types that are BOTH automerge-eligible and carrying a green internal status, so lock-file maintenance and everything else on that repo behave as before. That couples it to the first rule in this list: digest and pin updates also get `renovate/stability-days` from the top-level `minimumReleaseAge`, and are safe only because nothing grants them automerge, so if `automerge: true` is ever widened beyond minor and patch, widen this rule with it. DELETE THIS RULE when `staging` gains a required status check (reddoor-maintenance#545). It must stay LAST in packageRules, because later rules win.
